name: Jokim
overview: Jokim was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, known specifically as the son of Shelah, who was himself a son of Judah. His identity is grounded in his lineage within the tribe of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:22. Beyond this genealogical detail, Scripture does not provide additional notes about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Jokim means "YHWH lifts up," reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew meaning connected to the divine name YHWH. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:22, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jokim was the son of Shelah, who was a son of Judah, establishing Jokim's place within the Judahite lineage. No further family relationships are documented beyond this direct paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jokim’s significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah, which is foundational for understanding the heritage and tribal divisions of Israel. His mention in 1 Chronicles 4:22 contributes to the biblical record that traces the descendants of Judah, a tribe central to the Messianic lineage culminating in Jesus Christ. Jokim’s inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage through which the Messiah would come.
